# GitHub Actions Workflow Documentation

## [`Build.yaml`](Build.yaml)

This workflow runs whenever new changes are pushed to a pull request in order to validate the
pull request's changes.

This workflow is split up into several jobs, some of which run in parallel:

- Build & Test: Builds the Haskell code and compares the generated output with the stable folder.
  The generated artifacts are uploaded for use in later jobs.
- Haddock: Builds the Haddock documentation
- In parallel, after Build & Test succeeds:
  - Compile GOOL: Compiles the generated code (both the "gooltests" and the code generated by the examples).
  - LaTeX: Renders the generated LaTeX code into PDFs.
  - mdBook: Renders the generated mdBook markdown into HTML.
  - Jupyter: Renders the generated Jupyter notebooks into HTML.

These jobs only run if necessary. For instance, if there are no changes to stable, then only the Build & Test and Haddock
jobs will run. Changes to certain "build" files (such as the actions workflow or the Makefile) will cause all jobs to run,
as changes to these files can affect all parts of the workflow.

## [`Deploy.yaml`](Deploy.yaml)

This workflow runs on pushed to the main branch to ensure the branch builds and to deploy the website.

This workflow is split up into several jobs, some of which run in parallel:

- Build & Test: Builds the Haskell code and compares the generated output with the stable folder.
  Additionally, it generates certain artifacts (graphs and analysis) required for the website.
  The generated artifacts are uploaded for use in later jobs.
- Haddock: Builds the Haddock documentation. The generated documentation is uploaded for use in Prepare Deployment.
- In Parallel, after Build & Test succeeds:
  - Compile GOOL: Compiles the generated code (both the "gooltests" and the code generated by the examples).
  - Generate Documents: Generates final PDFs and HTML from LaTeX, mdBook and Jupyter sources.
- Prepare Deployment: After Haddock and Generate Documents are done, runs the `prepare_deployment.sh` script
  to prepare the website deployment. Uploads the ready-to-deploy website.
- Deploy: After Prepare Deployment, deploys the previously uploaded website to GitHub Pages.
- Cleanup Caches: After Build & Test and Haddock are done, clean up old stack-work caches. See below for more details.

## Caching in `Build.yaml` and `Deploy.yaml`

There are three different caches used:

1. The global stack cache, which caches `~/.stack`. This folder includes the GHC install, as
   well as compiled dependencies and other miscellaneous global stack files.
2. The `.stack-work` and `.hie` cache (for Build & Test). This cache contains Drasil's build artifacts,
   which change frequently. To prevent this cache from growing in size excessively,
   the cache is always saved in `Deploy.yaml` (but never restored), and always
   restored in `Build.yaml` (but never saved). This means that PRs will use the
   caches from the latest commit on main. This improves build times by allowing incremental builds
   without excessive cache usage.
3. The `.stack-work` and `.hie` cache (for Haddock). The same as above, but used in the Haddock
   jobs. Separating the build and Haddock caches seemed to give the fastest Haddock build times.

GitHub does not allow overwriting a cache key, so the Cleanup Caches job in Build & Test is necessary
to delete old stack-work caches. This job uses the GitHub CLI (`gh`) to automatically delete the
outdated caches.

## [`Lint.yaml`](Lint.yaml)

Runs whenever new changes are pushed to a pull request. Validates the changes using HLint, ShellCheck and `scripts/check_whitespace.sh`.

## [`Wiki.yaml`](Wiki.yaml)

Contains two jobs:

- Audit changes: Runs on pull requests to ensure any changes to the `wiki` folder are valid.
- Publish changes runs on main to synchronize the `wiki` folder to the `GitHub` wiki.
